title: App and user inventory in 3rd-Party App Governance: how apps get in, search, catalog sandboxing, bulk upload, custom views, client-ID exports

prose.text: {{population-methods}} The portal is in [[zia.app-governance]], and connecting platforms is in [[zia.app-governance.platforms]].

prose.label: Getting client IDs out of the platform.

population-methods.statement: The App Inventory page says the inventory can be automatically populated with apps by leveraging 3rd-Party App Governance's discovery capabilities, connecting SaaS platforms, manually uploading apps, and searching and adding from the 3rd-Party App Governance catalog.

quotes: You can automatically populate your inventory with apps by leveraging 3rd-Party App Governance’s discovery capabilities, connecting your various SaaS platforms to 3rd-Party App Governance, manually uploading apps, and by searching and adding from the 3rd-Party App Governance catalog.

inventory-columns.statement: The inventory list shows, for each app, Status, App Name (which opens the App Panel), Publisher, Platform, Origin, Marketplace (whether the app is publicly available in the marketplace), Users, Usage, Risk Score (which can be changed), Access Type, Access Level, Findings, Classification (which can be changed) and Automated Workflow. The apps report can be exported to a CSV file and a link to the list can be shared.

quotes: Status: The status of the app.
App Name: The name of the app. Click the app name to open the App Panel and further review it.
Publisher: The name of the app publisher.
Platform: The platform on which the app is supported.
Origin: The origin of the app. It can be one of the following:
Marketplace: Indicates whether the app is publicly available in the marketplace.
Users: The number of users using the app.
Usage: The app usage details.
Risk Score: The risk score for the app. You can change the risk score.
Access Type: The type of application access.
Access Level: The access level for the app.
Findings: The number of app findings.
Classification: The classification for the app. You can change the app's classification.
Automated Workflow: The automated workflow for the app.
Export the apps report to a CSV file.
Share a link of the list of apps in the inventory.

origin-values.statement: An app's origin is 1st Party (developed by the service provider integrated with 3rd-Party App Governance), 3rd Party (created by an external developer) or Internal App (developed for internal use within the organization).

quotes: 1st Party: The app is developed by the service provider integrated with 3rd-Party App Governance.
3rd Party: The app is created by an external developer.
Internal App: The app is developed for internal use within the organization.

filters.statement: More than one filter can be applied to the inventory. Filter options that do not yet exist in the organization can still be selected when creating new views and policies, and a new app that matches such a policy triggers it.

quotes: You can apply more than one filter to your inventory.

You can still select them when creating new views and policies. If a new app in your organization matches a policy, the policy is triggered and the filter options will be included in your organization.

custom-views.statement: A custom view is a saved search criterion that can be used as a rule to trigger a policy, and a view marked as a favorite gets a shortcut under Reports > Predefined Reports. If a view is already used as a trigger for a policy, the confirmation window highlights that when it is edited.

quotes: A custom view is a saved search criterion that you often reuse and require for your daily operations. You can use it as a rule to trigger a policy.
You can also mark the view as a favorite for easier access (this creates a shortcut to the view under Reports > Predefined Reports in the left-side navigation).
If this view is already used as a trigger (rule) for a policy, the confirmation window highlights that, so you might take it under advisement before editing such a view.

search.statement: Apps can be searched by name, client ID or publisher, in the App Inventory and the 3rd-Party App Governance app catalog. A filter selects inventory, catalog or both, and by default the search results from the inventory are displayed. Apps in the catalog that are not currently in the inventory appear in blue.

quotes: You can search for apps by name, client ID, or publisher to find results in the App Inventory and the 3rd-Party App Governance app catalog.
You can use the filter to view search results from the inventory, catalog, or both. By default, the search results from the inventory are displayed.
Apps in the catalog that are not currently in your inventory appear in blue.
evidence.after: To search for an app by name:

sandboxing.statement: An app that cannot be found in the inventory or catalog by name can be searched by client ID, and if it is still not found its client ID can be submitted for sandboxing. A summary shows the app as Pending and an email is received when it is uploaded. In a bulk upload, unrecognized apps are sent for sandboxing automatically and marked as pending.

quotes: If you cannot find the app in your inventory or 3rd-Party App Governance app catalog by name, you can search by client ID. If you still cannot find the app, you can submit the client ID for sandboxing.
A summary appears indicating that your app is Pending. You receive an email when your app is uploaded.
The same summary appears when you upload apps in bulk and 3rd-Party App Governance does not recognize one of the apps.
The unrecognized apps are sent for sandboxing automatically and marked as pending.

pre-vetting.statement: Depending on the organization's policy, users might request approval for apps, third-party integrations and browser extensions before installing them, and an admin can manually add a vetted app to the inventory and classify it for future records.

quotes: Depending on your organization's policy, users might request approval for apps, third-party integrations, and browser extensions before installing them.
You can also manually add it to your inventory and then classify the app for future records.

bulk-upload.statement: Apps are uploaded in bulk by entering the client IDs to add, separated by commas or any other delimiter, and apps in Pending mode are submitted for sandboxing.

quotes: enter the client IDs you want to add, separated by commas.
You can use any delimiter, not just a comma (,).
Apps in Pending mode are submitted for sandboxing.

client-id-export-atlassian.statement: Atlassian does not have a straightforward way of exporting the client IDs of all connected apps. The Zscaler team prepares a dedicated script that is shared with clients, which extracts app IDs for Atlassian JWT apps and OAuth apps and exports them to the CSV file atlassian_app_ids.csv.

quotes: Atlassian doesn't have a straightforward way of exporting a list of client IDs of all the apps connected to your environment.
The Zscaler team prepares a dedicated script that is shared with clients to help them extract the client IDs.
This script will extract app IDs for Atlassian JWT apps and OAuth apps, and export to a CSV file "atlassian_app_ids.csv"

client-id-export-azure.statement: The Microsoft Azure client ID export needs Administrator user credentials. After the CSV file is downloaded, app names are in the first column and client IDs are under App ID in the second column.

quotes: You must have Administrator user credentials to access this page.
After the CSV file is downloaded, the app names appear in the first column and the client IDs appear under App ID in the second column.

client-id-export-google.statement: In Google Workspace, admins can find all connected third-party apps under App Access Control, any Google user can find the apps with access to their account in account security settings, and the apps that accessed a Gmail inbox can be found in the inbox.

quotes: Google Workspace admins can navigate to App Access Control and find all the third-party apps connected to their Google environment.
Any Google user can navigate to account security settings and information and find the apps with access to their account.
In your Gmail inbox, you can find the apps that have accessed your inbox.

chrome-extensions-export.statement: The Chrome extensions export method for admins is supported if the organization's Chrome browsers are cloud-managed: enroll users' browsers to be cloud-managed using MDM software and turn on Chrome browser reporting. The page's separate method for a user starts by opening Google Chrome and entering chrome://system/ into the address bar.

quotes: This method is supported if the Chrome browsers in your organization are cloud-managed.
Enroll your user’s browsers to be cloud-managed using an MDM software.
Turn on Chrome browser reporting.
To export extensions as a user:
Open Google Chrome, and enter chrome://system/ into the address bar.

user-inventory.statement: The User Inventory shows all the enabled users in 3rd-Party App Governance, with columns that include Apps (the number of apps enabled for the user) and Role. Users can be searched by email, display name or job title and the users report exported to a CSV file.

quotes: The User Inventory enables you to view and manage all the enabled users in 3rd-Party App Governance.
Search for a user by email, display name, or job title.
Export the users report to a CSV file.
Apps: The number of apps enabled for the user.
Role: The role of the user.

user-panel-tabs.statement: The User Panel has tabs that show the user's sign-in activities, the top apps and the user's permissions, and an activities view that can be filtered by User Activity, Security Event and Findings.

quotes: View information about the user's sign-in activities.
View information about top apps and user's permissions.
Filter your search by User Activity, Security Event, and Findings.

user-panel-files-tab.statement: The Files tab of the User Panel shows the Data Loss Prevention (DLP) violations for the user's files over a selected period, classified by document type. It is in limited availability, and needs a license for SaaS Security Data at Rest Scanning DLP with the DLP scan previously configured.

quotes: View information about the Data Loss Prevention (DLP) violations for the user's files over a selected period of time. The DLP violations are classified based on the document type.
This feature is in limited availability.
To view the information on the Files tab, you must have a license for SaaS Security Data at Rest Scanning DLP and the DLP scan must be previously configured.
